questions.stem: A 53-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with complaints of feeling like the room is spinning, dizziness, decreased hearing, ringing in the ears, and fullness in both ears. He states that the symptoms have been occurring episodically but increasing in frequency. The ringing in his ears was not present initially but has become more prominent. He denies any recent ear infections or trauma. He is not taking any medications. On examination, he is noted to have low-frequency hearing loss. The remainder of the examination is normal. After a complete workup is done, the patient is diagnosed with Ménière disease. What part of the vestibular system detects angular acceleration and rotation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Semicircular canals
  • Angular acceleration and rotation are seen in Semicircular canals.
  • Ménière disease is a syndrome of recurrent attacks of vertigo and tinnitus associated with hearing loss. The underlying pathophysiology is a disorder of fluid balance within the endolymphatic system, leading to the degeneration of vestibular and cochlear hair cells.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 182–183; 215

questions.stem: Otoliths have which of the following properties?

options.label: A
options.text: They contain kinocilia and cation channels that are opened when pulled by extracellular filaments.

options.label: B
options.text: They are located only in the saccule and utricle.

options.label: C
options.text: They are located only in the semicircular canals.

options.label: D
options.text: They bend stereocilia toward but not away from the kinocilium.

questions.answerText: They are located only in the saccule and utricle.
questions.solutionHtml:
They are located only in the saccule and utricle.
  • Otoliths are located in the otolithic organs, the saccule and utricle, not in the three semicircular canals.
  • They are pulled by gravity against the gelatinous cap containing stereocilia, which can bend either toward or away from the kinocilium. This bending preferentially transduces linear acceleration rather than angular acceleration (which is transduced by hair cells in the semicircular canals).


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 182–183; 215

questions.stem: At a first-grade parent-teacher conference, the teacher of a 6-year-old boy indicates that the boy seems to have difficulty hearing. His parents take him to the pediatrician, who refers the boy to an otolaryngologist. The boy is found to have a significant hearing deficit accompanying a middle ear infection that also involves the middle ear bones. Which of the following is the primary function of the middle ear bones?
questions.solutionHtml:
To amplify sounds
  • In the case of the 6-year-old boy with a middle ear infection, the infection likely caused inflammation and fluid buildup in the middle ear, which can interfere with the ability of the ossicles to transmit sound waves effectively. This can result in a significant hearing deficit.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 206

questions.stem: The morning after a rock concert, a 20-year-old college student notices difficulty hearing his professor during a lecture. The physician at the Student Health Center suspects possible damage to his hair cells by the loud music. Depolarization of the hair cells in the cochlea is caused primarily by the flow of which of the following?

options.label: C
options.text: Cl– out of the hair cell

questions.solutionHtml:
K+ into the hair cell
  • The depolarization of hair cells in the cochlea is caused primarily by the flow of positively charged potassium ions (K+) into the hair cells.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 171–183.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is admitted to the hospital for evaluation after demonstrating signs and symptoms of a stroke. Subsequent CT scans, perceptual tests, and a neurological examination provide evidence for impairment of the otolith pathways. The otolith organs (utricle and saccule) are responsible for which of the following?

options.label: B
options.text: Detecting the position of the head in space

questions.answerText: Detecting the position of the head in space
questions.solutionHtml:
Detecting the position of the head in space
  • The otolith organs provide information about the position of the head with respect to gravity.
  • When the head is bent away from its normal upright position, otoliths (small calcium carbonate crystals within the utricle and saccule) are pulled downward by gravity.
  • The crystals bend the stereocilia on the hair cells, causing the hair cells to depolarize.
  • Depolarization of the hair cells stimulates the vestibular nerve fibers. Bending the head in different directions causes different otoliths to move.
  • Therefore, the particular group of vestibular nerve fibers that are stimulated signals the direction in which the head bends.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 171–172, 183–184.
